newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Tribal rebels extend truce unilaterally.
newsitem.headline: Tribal rebels extend truce unilaterally.

text.p: Separatist tribal rebels seeking autonomy for Bangladesh's southeastern Chittagong Hill Tracts, have unilaterally extended a truce until the end of this month, rebel sources said on Monday.
They told reporters the truce had been extended until November 30.

The government earlier said it had expired on October 31 and officials in Chittagong, headquarters of the counter-insurgency operations, said they had received no communication yet from the rebel Shati Bahini (peace force).
"We still don't know of any Shanti Bahini decision about extending the truce. We so far only know that the latest ceasefire expired on Thursday," one official said on Monday.
The truce had been extended for one month at a time since early this year while both sides agreed to hold peace talks, which have so far produced no agreement.
The armed insurgency began in 1973 after Bangladesh rejected Shanti Bahini's demand for political autonomy for the 5,500 sq-mile (14,200 sq-km) Hill Tracts, bordering India and Burma.
The tribal rebels also want some 300,000 Bengali-speaking settlers to be expelled from the region.

Officials say more than 8,500 people including rebels, soldiers and civilians, have been killed in the protracted insurgency, which has also forced thousands of tribal families to seek refuge in India.
